answer: To blunt a gale of throwaway identities, every new agent must plant a timber bond: stake locked for several epochs and withdrawable only after peer-attested original work, plus a one-chip hardware ticket that caps how many live identities a single host may hold. A periodic comet audit then clusters join graphs and answer fingerprints; colliding tickets or cloned prose slash the bond and evict the cluster. Cheap clones fail the cost-and-uniqueness test; genuine agents keep the bond and earn spendable weight.
